item.title: A Guide to Student Discounts in Boston
item.description: By now, you probably know that Boston is one of America’s biggest college towns, which undoubtedly comes with its perks. Local stores, restaurants, and organizations that you know and love offer a variety of discounts, helping students get the most out of their beloved city.

item.title: BC’s Week of Dance Captivates, Leaving Audience Wanting More
item.description: Amidst strobing lights and the audience’s rising anticipation, Robsham Theater erupted with cheers at the opening of Boston College’s Week of Dance Saturday performance. Parents and students filled the seats early, calling out to their loved ones backstage long before the lights dimmed.

item.title: Fringe, Houndstooth, and More: Fashion Trend Predictions for 2026
item.description: As much as we all hope to cultivate an individual style above fast fashion cycles, the changing of the calendar brings forth a new rotation of what’s considered “in.” Like clockwork, the sales racks—in-person and online—will overflow with the latest trends, despite your efforts to tune out influencers commanding you to “run to your nearest mall ASAP!”

item.title: BC Closes and Cancels Classes Due to Winter Storm
item.description: Boston College will close Monday due to the snowstorm that has brought over a foot of snow to campus, the University announced this evening.

item.title: Enhanced Version of Newton 311 App Brings Convenience to User Experience
item.description: Newton has rolled out a new version of its 311 app—a digital service for residents to report non-emergency issues—upgrading the technology to make communication with the city more efficient and accessible.

item.title: Man Faces Assault To Murder Charges After Allegedly Trying To Run Over Ex-Girlfriend at The Shops at Chestnut Hill
item.description: A 26-year-old man is facing two assault to murder charges and several other felony and misdemeanor charges after he allegedly attempted to run over his former girlfriend and her current boyfriend at The Shops at Chestnut Hill on Boylston Street last weekend.

item.title: Suzuki School of Newton Approved for $600,000 in Funding Toward Major Renovation
item.description: The Suzuki School of Newton was unanimously approved for $600,000 in Community Preservation Act (CPA) Historic Resource funding to help fund a $2.5 million school renovation at a joint meeting of the Finance Committee and Zoning and Planning Committee on Monday.

item.title: UGBC Addresses Agora Portal Issues, Blocked from UHS Online Booking Initiative
item.description: The UGBC Senate voiced optimism Tuesday night about a plan to reorganize Boston College’s Agora Portal to address existing issues and make the platform more accessible for students.
